key_insight: Fine-tuned transformer models, especially FLAN-T5-Large, can detect social isolation and social support cues in clinical notes with high accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This could help care teams identify older adults at risk for poor social connectedness earlier from EHR text, supporting targeted outreach and stratification.
method: Annotated clinical note spans for social isolation, social support, and non-isolation cues
Fine-tuned FLAN-T5-Large, BERT, RoBERTa, and Gemma-2-2B on notes from 326,847 adults aged 50+
Used structured prompting and compared Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and Macro-F1
evidence_signal: FLAN-T5-Large had the best overall performance with Macro-F1 0.92 ± 0.04, outperforming Gemma-2-2B (0.89 ± 0.10), RoBERTa (0.80 ± 0.21), and BERT (0.77 ± 0.17).
watch_item: Performance may vary across sites and note styles, so real-world deployment still needs external validation and careful handling of false positives, negations, and ambiguous context.
paper_title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Detecting Social Isolation from Unstructured Clinical Notes
